title: A finite coproduct of etale morphisms is etale
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $(u_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $V=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ be their coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and let $u:V\to X$ be the morphism whose restriction to $U_i$ is $u_i$. Then $u$ is etale.

source.place: Morphisms, Definition Tag 02GI and Lemma Tag 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize), locality of etaleness on the source, applied to the open-and-closed coproduct summands

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], each coprojection $\iota_i:U_i\to V$ is an open immersion, its image is open and closed, the images are pairwise disjoint, and they cover $V$. The restriction of $u$ to the image of $\iota_i$ is therefore the morphism $u_i$, by the defining equation $u\circ\iota_i=u_i$ of the induced coproduct morphism. Since the images form an open cover of $V$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] applied to $u:V\to X$ says that $u$ is etale exactly when all these restrictions are etale; they are etale by hypothesis. This also covers the empty family, whose coproduct is empty and whose open-cover condition is vacuous.
